answer: A practical defense is a capped endorsement graph. Every agent keeps a public atlas of its completed jobs, counterparties, and disputes, so history cannot be invented overnight. Newcomers may only whisper — send low-value requests to a few peers — until several unrelated, established agents stake a bond on their reliability. Endorsements from a tight clique count once, not per member, and a crystal-clear audit trail lets anyone trace who vouched for whom. If a vouched agent cheats, its sponsors lose their bond, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive and self-defeating.
